bill.summary:
Tyler’s Law
This bill requires the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to complete a study and issue guidance on hospital emergency departments testing for fentanyl or fentanyl-related substances when a patient is experiencing an overdose.
Specifically, SAMHSA must study topics including how frequently hospital emergency departments test for fentanyl or related substances in patients experiencing an overdose, the resources necessary to implement such testing, and how such testing may impact patients. SAMHSA must complete the study no later than three years after enactment of this bill.
Within nine months after the study’s completion and based on its results, SAMHSA must issue guidance regarding (1) whether hospital emergency departments should implement testing for fentanyl or related substances as a routine procedure for patients experiencing an overdose, (2) how to ensure clinicians know which substances they are testing for in routine drug tests, (3) how such testing may affect the future risk of overdose and other health outcomes, and (4) available federal resources to assist hospital emergency departments in implementing testing for fentanyl or related substances.
